connections.why: Classical-era forms develop directly out of Baroque procedures and textures
Romantic orchestral music expands the structures established in the Classical era
Romantic orchestral language is the foundation of much stage and screen scoring
Setting words to music underpins song in musicals, opera and film
Much dance music around the world is played by small traditional ensembles
Studying Baroque harmony and counterpoint models the writing of a notated score
Classical form and phrasing give structural models for a composed score
The 'Music and words' area is one brief option for the second composition
'Music for dance' is a candidate-defined brief option for composition 2
'Music for small ensemble' is a brief option, drawing on ensemble study
'Music for stage and screen' is a candidate-defined brief for composition 2
Aural awareness of style sharpens stylistic interpretation in solo performance
Studying ensemble textures informs balance and blend in group performance
Solo technique is the foundation for playing accurately within an ensemble
Knowing an instrument well helps write idiomatic, playable composed parts
Ensemble experience makes composing for combined instruments more idiomatic
